eye.because: The frames form one clean run of changes. B (right of the lane) is a plain house with windows and a door in Z. In Y its ground floor is a shuttered shopfront with a fascia, double door and signboard. In W and X it also has a glazed veranda with a balcony built onto its side wall. A has a big shop window in Z, Y and W, but in X the shop window is gone and ordinary house windows stand in its place, so X is last. D at the back has boarded-up windows in Z and Y and open windows in W and X, so it changes between Y and W. The order of changes is the same in all four views; what I cannot settle is which way time runs. I read it as things accruing: shop inserted, then extension built, then shop turned back to a home, D reopened. Run backwards it would be an extension demolished and a house closed up, which I find less likely. The years are rough guesses from the wood cladding, sash windows, plate-glass shopfront and glazed veranda; I put them 20 years apart with little to anchor them.

street.because: The changes here are on C (left) and D (right, on the rock). D's gable windows are boarded with crossed planks in W and Z and open, glazed windows in X and Y, so W and Z come before X and Y. C's windows are renewed in stages like a repair run. In W the small gable window is bare. In Z and X it has a sill with little feet. In Y it has that sill, and the two front windows also have lintel and sill trim. That gives W, then Z, then X, then Y. X and Z differ in D (boarded in Z, open in X). This matches the order I found in the eye and city views, because D reopens at the same point where B gets its extension. Direction is read as windows being renewed and D being reoccupied; a reversed reading (trim being lost) seems unnatural. The years are rough guesses.

12m.because: D's windows are boarded in X and W and open in Z and Y. The small dark house E at the top of the lane has the opposite pattern: open windows in X and W, boarded in Z and Y. So X and W are first and Z and Y last. C's gable window is bare in X, but has a sill and trim in W, Z and Y. Only Y has the lintel and sill trim on C's front windows, so Y is last and X first. That fixes the order as X, W, Z, Y, which matches the C and D stages in the street view. Years are rough guesses, 20 years apart.

city.because: Seen from above, only A and B change. In X, B is a plain house with ground-floor windows, flower boxes and a door canopy. In W the ground floor is a blank shopfront. In Y and Z the same shopfront stands and a balcony and veranda extension has been added along the left end of B. A has a shop window in X, W and Y. In Z it has two ordinary windows instead, so Z is last. This is the same sequence as the eye view. I take the direction as growth first (shop, then extension), with A's shop closing last. The reverse is possible, which is why I am only fairly sure. Years are rough guesses.
